facts.text: Willowbrook is best known as the former site of the Willowbrook State School, a state institution for people with intellectual disabilities that opened in 1947.
In 1972, a young Geraldo Rivera broadcast an undercover investigation of the severely overcrowded Willowbrook State School, revealing deplorable conditions and sparking national outrage.
The Willowbrook exposé led to the landmark New York State Association for Retarded Children v. Rockefeller lawsuit and consent decree, a turning point in the national movement for disability rights.
The College of Staten Island, part of the City University of New York, now occupies the former Willowbrook campus, with several original buildings still in use.
The Staten Island Greenbelt, one of New York City's largest areas of continuous natural land, borders Willowbrook and offers miles of hiking and nature trails.
